answer: Each challenge commits to a future drand quicknet pulse, whose threshold-BLS output remains unpredictable until the scheduled round and becomes publicly verifiable afterward. A sybil swarm therefore cannot precompute valid responses, choose favorable identities, or farm work offline: each attempt must await the beacon reveal and bind to the committed instance through a commit-reveal exchange. A walnut-named vertex or nectar-tagged token cannot substitute for that fresh cryptographic dependency.
